doc.title: Denny Zeitlin interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Early psychotherapy and the path to medicine
summary: Prompted by a career question, he recalls playing therapist on the playground, his analyst uncle, his mother's psychological radar, and wanting to be a psychiatrist.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah you could actually get tossed out of the practice rooms in some of the conservatories — who said it, Don Menza said “playing swing was a misdemeanor and playing bebop was a felony.” Oh gosh. Well did you come to a point ever when, in your late teens or whatever and maybe with your parents where you had a career decision to make? Was there ever a thought of trying to make a living as a jazz musician? And when did your interest in medicine start?

Well I think — I know that my music preceded my medical interest because I really was playing around at age two or three. But it was only a few years later that I started practicing psychotherapy without a license on the playground.
